ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an LM317 regulated power supply circuit. Pin 3 of the LM317 is connected to the positive input terminal, pin 2 is connected to the positive output terminal, and pin 1 is the adjustment terminal. Resistor R1 is vertically connected between the output terminal node and the adjustment terminal node; variable resistor Rp is connected between the adjustment terminal node and the lower common ground line, so Rp is the lower-arm adjustable resistor in the LM317 output voltage formula. The input and output filter capacitors can also be seen in the figure, but they do not determine the DC output set value. Reasoning: The LM317 approximately satisfies Uo = 1.25(1 + R2/R1), where R2 = Rp. The problem states R1 = 200 Ω, and the maximum Rp is 1 kΩ = 1000 Ω; the input voltage is sufficiently large, so it is not limited by the voltage drop. To make the output voltage maximum, take Rp = 1000 Ω. Calculate Uo,max = 1.25 × (1 + 1000/200) = 1.25 × 6 = 7.5 V.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify R1 as the upper feedback resistor between OUT and ADJ and Rp as the lower adjustable resistor between ADJ and ground. From the text, use R1 = 200 Ω and Rp max = 1 kΩ. Since input voltage is sufficiently large, dropout does not limit the output. Set R2 = Rp = 1000 Ω and compute Uo,max = 1.25(1 + 1000/200) = 1.25 × 6 = 7.5 V.
